question: Let c(n) be the number of cubes mod n. For each fixed K, the n with at most K distinct prime factors and 3c(n) = n + 2 are finitely many, with an explicit bound on n in terms of K; and the same for the second equation (p + 2)c(B) = pB + 2 with p prime, p = 1 mod 6.
general_form: A multiplicative function f with f(n)/n close to 1 at every prime, and an exact rational target f(n) = (n + r)/d: bound the solutions with a fixed number of prime factors.

instances.how: After the local bounds, every term other than 1 and the primes 1 mod 6 solves one of the two equations; finiteness for each K plus a search would leave only the unbounded-K case.
Squares mod n with target n/3 + 1; closed because the factor 3 pins the product. Test case for any general argument.
Squares mod n with target n/4 + 1. Test case.
phi(n) | n - 1. Finiteness for fixed K is known there (recalled: Pomerance 1977, n < K^(2^K); citation not yet checked).

why_easier: Fixing K turns an open classification into a finite-dimensional one: the largest prime factor is bounded from the smaller ones by the exact equation, by the argument used for Lehmer's problem. A Lehmer-type argument exists; the original question (all K) stays open.

check.description: work/cores/a123365_scan.py: all n < 10^7 with 3c(n) = n + 2, grouped by number of distinct prime factors.
check.result: Only n = 1 and the 332194 primes p = 1 mod 6 below 10^7; no solution with 2 or more prime factors.

tests.leverage: reduces OEIS-A123365; same shape as A123722, A123723, Lehmer

notes: Speculative until a proof for K = 2 is written. Next: prove K = 2 for 3c(n) = n + 2 (two primes q, r = 2 mod 3 with exponents), in Lean if the bound is small. 2026-11-05: K = 2 done in Lean (OEIS/A123365, closed forms of c as hypotheses) by a mod-q valuation argument, not the Lehmer-type one. K >= 3 obstacle: the prime 1 mod 3 sets the target itself and exponents are unbounded (c(q^e)/q^e cycles with e mod 3). Lehmer fixed-K finiteness proved in Lean (FAM/lehmer-totient).

question: Formalise in Lean + Mathlib a Brun or Selberg upper-bound sieve strong enough to give #{p <= x : p and p + h prime} << x/(log x)^2 * prod_{q | h, q odd} (q-1)/(q-2), uniformly in even h.
general_form: An upper-bound sieve for k-tuples of linear forms in Mathlib.

instances.how: Growth of |a(n)|^(1/n) needs the uniform prime-pair bound (attempt 2026-11-05).
Needs an O(n/log^2 n) bound for Goldbach representations, the same sieve.
Brun: sum of reciprocals of twin primes converges, from the same prime-pair upper bound.

why_easier: Upper-bound sieves are classical and unconditional (Brun 1919, Selberg 1947), and Mathlib already has the Selberg sieve framework (Mathlib/NumberTheory/SelbergSieve.lean: upper-bound sieves, Lambda^2 weights, diagonalised main term). The remaining work is the application to prime pairs: choice of sieve level and the error-term estimate.

check.description: Both blocked attempts name this exact bound as the only missing step.
check.result: Confirmed by the attempt records for OEIS-A187011 and the Lean notes of OEIS-A215462.

tests.leverage: settles parts of A187011 and A215462; likely more prime-gap OEIS claims

notes: Checked 2026-11-05: Mathlib's SelbergSieve.lean (Mellendijk 2024) gives the framework but no twin-prime bound. Brun's theorem (a famous-round target) needs the same step, so one formalisation serves three items. 2026-11-05: answered in Lean with K(h)^2 = (h/phi(h))^2 in place of the singular series (FAM/twin-primes, pairCount_le_log); applying it to A187011 and A215462 is the next step. 2026-11-05: applied; OEIS-A187011 growth part (A187011_growth) and OEIS-A215462 conjecture 2 (A215462_conj2, via a Goldbach sieve with one factor of K(2n)) are now full Lean proofs. Leverage test met: three items settled by one tool.

question: For every n >= 2, the number of singular symmetric n x n matrices with entries +-1 equals 2^n times the number of singular symmetric (n-1) x (n-1) matrices with entries 0/1.
general_form: Transfer singularity counts between sign and 0/1 symmetric ensembles by a diagonal congruence and one Schur complement (A = D [[1, 1^T],[1, J - 2B]] D style), so questions about one ensemble become questions about the other.

instances.how: The uniform-sign rate (1/2+o(1))^n is proved for the 0/1 ensemble after this transfer.

instances.problem: OEIS counts of singular symmetric 0/1 and +-1 matrices
instances.how: Any OEIS pair counting these two families satisfies a(n) = 2^n b(n-1); a conjectured link between such entries would be settled.
A118990(n) = 2^n A086906(n-1); holds for all listed terms n = 2..10 (checked 2026-11-05), not stated in either entry.

why_easier: An exact finite identity with an elementary proof (normalise first row/column by a sign diagonal, take a Schur complement), while the problems served are asymptotic.

check.description: work/openai/src/check_sym_sign.py: brute force over all symmetric matrices with exact Bareiss determinants, n <= 6.
check.result: Identity holds for n = 2..6: +-1 singular counts 4, 32, 512, 15872, 907008; 0/1 singular counts (n-1 = 1..5) 1, 4, 32, 496, 14172. Independently rechecked n = 2..5 by brute force; matches OEIS data A118990 vs A086906 for n = 2..10.

question: If real numbers c_n satisfy c_{2n} >= c_n - e_n (and a matching upper comparison c_{2n} <= c_n + e_n for the limsup) with sum_k e_{2^k n0} finite, plus a monotonicity or Lipschitz bound between n and n+1, then c_n converges. Which OEIS growth-constant conjectures admit such a comparison?
general_form: Near-superadditivity along dyadic sizes with summable errors implies convergence (a de Bruijn-Erdos type lemma), used with an interpolation or concatenation inequality supplying e_n.

instances.how: Convergence of the finite-size k-SAT threshold centres.
Pressure of orthogonally invariant spin glasses via interpolation against independent subsystems.

instances.problem: OEIS "a(n)^(1/n) converges" conjectures for near-supermultiplicative counts
instances.how: A concatenation map from two size-n objects into one size-2n object, losing a summable factor, gives the hypothesis.

why_easier: The lemma is deterministic and short; the problems need only the comparison inequality, which is often a concatenation argument.

check.description: Not run. Check = apply to a known case (e.g. self-avoiding walk counts, where submultiplicativity is exact) and to one OEIS conjecture.

question: A search-and-compose tool: enumerate small Boolean functions (or gadgets/matrices) and compute the pair of measures that compose multiplicatively (s and bs at 0; retained variance and cell degree; tensor-power application count); report seeds whose ratio beats the target and the exponent their iteration gives.
general_form: Finite seed + composition lemma -> power separation.

instances.how: A seed with bs(f,0) > s(f)^2 gives a superquadratic sensitivity/block-sensitivity separation by composition.
A gadget retaining more variance than its degree cost gives unbounded Gopalan-Servedio ratio.
A finite tensor saving for a small nonmonomial matrix gives sub-(n log n) Fourier transforms.

instances.problem: Sensitivity vs block sensitivity exponent (is bs <= s^3?)
instances.how: Better seeds give better lower exponents.

why_easier: Each seed check is a finite computation on a few variables; the composition lemmas are already proved in the families.

check.description: Not run. Check = recompute s and bs for known separating functions (Rubinstein bs = s^2/2) and exhaustively for n <= 5.

notes: The 132 seed condition uses bs at the input 0 but global s; check the exact statement in the PDF before searching.

question: What is the least r for which some intersecting r-partite r-uniform hypergraph has covering number r (violating Ryser's bound r-1)? Known: the bound holds for small r (r <= 5 per the 162 summary agent); 162 gives counterexamples at r = q+1 for large primes q.
general_form: Smallest parameter at which a finite-geometry modification (merge two parallel lines, split two others) beats a covering bound.

instances.how: Its construction works for large primes q; small q would locate the threshold.
Determines the exact range where the intersecting case holds.

instances.problem: Gyarfas monochromatic tree-cover conjecture (r-1 trees cover an r-edge-coloured K_n)
instances.relation: same threshold by the classical equivalence
instances.how: The intersecting case of Ryser is equivalent to the tree-cover statement, so the least r is the same.

why_easier: For each fixed small r it is a finite search; the affine-plane construction for q = 5, 7, 8 gives candidate instances checkable by ILP.

check.description: Not run. Check = build the 162 construction for q = 5, 7 (needs the exact modification from the PDF) and compute tau by ILP.

tests.leverage: Ryser intersecting threshold and Gyarfas threshold (equivalent), sharpens 162

notes: Equivalence Ryser-intersecting <-> Gyarfas tree cover is classical (recalled; citation not checked). Known small-r results recalled, not checked.

core-Lean table scan over 10^6 numbers failed for kernel speed; solved instead by a Mathlib bound
